method: Researched 2026-10-19 with a read-only fetcher sending the User-Agent lexflow-research/0.1 (https://github.com/alibama/lexflow), honouring robots.txt, at least 1.5 seconds between requests to one host and 5 seconds for web.archive.org. www.ci.staunton.va.us answered HTTP 403 to the first request and was not retried: every city page and PDF was read from its newest Internet Archive capture (CDX lookup, newest 200 capture first; capture timestamps and URLs are recorded per page). deq.virginia.gov answered 403 and was read from captures. Other hosts (law.lis.virginia.gov, vdh.virginia.gov, abc.virginia.gov, columbiagasva.com, stauntonbusiness.com, ecode360.com) were read live. No browser was used, no form was submitted, no account was created, no portal was logged into. PDFs were converted with pdftotext. The local quote index (Docker) was down, so every quote in the process files is marked source: official-page; a local check matched all 324 quotes against the fetched texts (whitespace and curly quotes normalised) or against quotes carried over from the verified building_permit_residential, bpol_business_license and meals_tax_filing files. The Staunton City Code on eCode360 was read for section numbers and paraphrase only and is never quoted (General Code's terms); its fee amounts (§ 15.10.120 building permits, § 15.25.055 fire permits, § 18.220.020 zoning) are reported as figures with the section cited. Web search (four queries) was used only to find page URLs and the eCode360 node ids; nothing from search snippets is quoted.

open_questions_for_offices: Planning & Zoning: which listed use a hot shop with gallery and classes is closest to in the building's district; whether it is permitted by right, on review (special use permit) or not at all; whether furnace flues, exhaust stacks and gas equipment visible from the street in a historic district are 'screening of mechanical equipment' (staff review) or exterior alterations (Commission); the Certificate of Appropriateness fee.

Building Services: the occupancy group(s) and fire protection requirements for the hot shop, gallery and classroom; whether the Fire Marshal reviews gas and cylinder storage at plan review; commercial trade permit processing time.

Fire Marshal's Office: which SFPC Table 107.2 permits beyond LP-gas and hazardous materials the office requires for oxygen and flammable gas cylinders, torches, the furnace and glory hole (industrial oven?), hot work and public classes (place of assembly, open flame), and their fees; which local board hears fire code appeals.

Commissioner of the Revenue: classification of a mixed retail, teaching and manufacturing studio (one combined license at the highest rate or several); whether the studio is a manufacturer for the wholesale exemption and the machinery-and-tools class; how meals tax registration is done.

Public Works and City Engineer: the current water and sewer fee schedule and the meter size a cold shop and cafe need; whether the cold shop's discharge needs a pretreatment wastewater survey, permit or solids trap; commercial account deposit.
Columbia Gas of Virginia: availability and cost of service for the furnace and glory hole load at the address (main extension or larger meter).
DEQ Valley Regional Office: whether a gas-fired glass furnace is 'fuel burning equipment' under 9VAC5-80-1105 B or a process unit judged by emission rate, and whether any toxics screening applies.
Health District: the Foodservice Permit Application form and local lead times for temporary food permits.
Virginia ABC: whether banquet licenses fit a for-profit studio's ticketed sip-and-blow nights, and the application fees and documents.
Economic Development: Enterprise Zone, Opportunity Zone and C-PACE eligibility for a given building and the application process.
